header.name: Topics in Functional Analysis: Operator Theory on Hilbert spaces
header.description:
The course aims to provide an introduction to the structure of Hilbert spaces and linear operators on them. The focus will be on definitions, fundamental theorems, and complete proofs, supplemented throughout by examples and exercises that build both intuition and technical skill.

The course is broadly divided into three chapters --- Chapter 0, Chapter 1 and Chapter 2. The primary aim of this course is to make available to students the results in Chapters 1 and 2; Chapter 0 is a tragically brief primer on the geometry of Hilbert spaces and is there to prepare the way to the latter chapters.

Next, we turn to operators on Hilbert spaces in Chapter 1. We study, in detail, the invertible operators and then introduce the Hilbert space adjoint, which leads to the study of invariant and reducing subspaces. We examine important classes of operators. A detailed study of projections is undertaken, including their relationship with closed subspaces and the lattice structure they form.

Finally, in Chapter 2, we develop the spectral theory of compact operators. After studying finite-rank and compact operators on normed linear spaces and Hilbert spaces, we introduce diagonalizable operators and prove the spectral theorem for compact operators. We explore functional calculus for compact normal operators and the concept of unitary equivalence, highlighting the close relationship between operators and matrices. This part emphasizes how abstract operator-theoretic results lead to concrete spectral decompositions, providing a bridge between finite-dimensional linear algebra and infinite-dimensional analysis.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to define and apply fundamental geometric structures of Hilbert spaces, including inner products, orthogonality, and projections. They will be able to demonstrate foundational understanding of Hilbert space geometry and analyse it using tools such as the Gram–Schmidt process and the Riesz Representation Theorem. Students will also formulate equivalence of Hilbert spaces and justify that a Hilbert space is determined, up to isomorphism, by its dimension.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to classify and differentiate major classes of operators, including bounded, compact, self-adjoint, positive, normal, unitary, isometries, and partial isometries. They will compute adjoint operators and establish the correspondence between subspaces and projections.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to explain the spectral theorem and its assumptions. They will analyze compact operators as limits of finite-rank operators and extend finite-dimensional diagonalization results to the compact setting.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will identify spectra, eigenvalues, and eigenbases of compact self-adjoint operators, apply functional calculus to compact normal operators, and interpret operators as infinite-dimensional matrices.

lecture_topics: Chapter 0: The geometry of Hilbert spaces
Reisz representation theorem for Hilbert spaces
The direct sum of Hilbert spaces
The (Hilbert space) adjoint of an operator
Normal; Self-adjoint; Positive Operators --- Definitions, characterization and elementary results
Projections - a special class of positive operators (revisited)
The lattice of projections: Characterization of Orthogonal Projections, Projections and subspaces, Sums of projections, Products and differences of projections, Infima and suprema of projections
Chapter 3: The spectral theorem for compact operators
Finite rank operators between normed linear spaces
Compact operators between normed linear spaces
Functional calculus for compact normal operators
Unitary equivalence for compact normal operators
